sanskrit: etat pṛcchāmi te vidvann abhivādya praṇamya ca ātmanaś ca tapobhāgyaṃ mahābhāgyaṃ tathaiva ca
english: This I ask of you, O learned one, after saluting and bowing low: the blessing of your austerity, and your great good fortune as well.

sanskrit: pṛthag ācaratas tāta pṛthag ātmani cātmanoḥ alpāntaram ahaṃ manye viśiṣṭam api vā tvayā
english: Though we two practice apart, dear one, and each lives within his own self, I reckon the difference between us small—or, it may be, that you surpass me.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca aticchedātivādābhyāṃ smayo 'yaṃ samupāgataḥ asatyaṃ vedavacanaṃ kasmād vedo 'nṛtaṃ vadet
english: Vyāsa said: This smile of mine arose at excessive cutting-down and excessive speech. False is the word of the Veda?—why should the Veda utter an untruth?

sanskrit: trīṇy eva tu padāny āhuḥ puruṣasyottamaṃ vratam na druhyec caiva dadyāc ca satyaṃ caiva paraṃ vadet idānīṃ caiva naḥ kṛtyaṃ purastāc ca paraṃ smṛtam
english: Three steps alone, they say, make up a man's highest vow: he should do no injury, he should give, and he should speak supreme truth. This is our duty now, and it is remembered as the highest hereafter as well.

sanskrit: alpo 'pi tādṛśo dāyo bhavaty uta mahāphalaḥ tṛṣitāya ca yad dattaṃ hṛdayenānasūyatā
english: Even a small gift of such a kind becomes great in its fruit—that which is given to one who craves it, from a heart that bears no grudging.

sanskrit: tṛṣitas tṛṣitāya tvaṃ dattvaitad aśanaṃ mama ajaiṣīr mahato lokān mahāyajñair ivābhibho ato dānapavitreṇa prīto 'smi tapasaiva ca
english: Yourself hungering, you gave this food of mine to one who hungered, and thereby you have won, O mighty one, vast worlds, as though by great sacrifices. Therefore I am pleased—by the sanctity of your gift, and by your austerity too.

sanskrit: puṇyasyaiva hi te gandhaḥ puṇyasyaiva ca darśanam puṇyaś ca vāti gandhas te manye karmavidhānataḥ
english: For your very fragrance is that of merit, and the very sight of you is meritorious; meritorious is the scent that breathes from you—and that, I think, comes from the ordering of your deeds.

sanskrit: adhikaṃ mārjanāt tāta tathaivāpy anulepanāt śubhaṃ sarvapavitrebhyo dānam eva paraṃ bhavet
english: More than any scrubbing clean, dear one, and more than any anointing—auspicious beyond all purifiers—giving alone becomes the supreme.

sanskrit: yānīmāny uttamānīha vedoktāni praśaṃsasi teṣāṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ dānam iti me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: Of all those highest things declared in the Veda which you here extol, giving is the most excellent—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: dānakṛdbhiḥ kṛtaḥ panthā yena yānti manīṣiṇaḥ te hi prāṇasya dātāras teṣu dharmaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: The path is made by the givers of gifts, by which the wise go their way; for they are the givers of life itself, and in them dharma stands firm.

sanskrit: yathā vedāḥ svadhītāś ca yathā cendriyasaṃyamaḥ sarvatyāgo yathā ceha tathā dānam anuttamam
english: As the Vedas well studied, as the restraint of the senses, as total renunciation here—even so is giving unsurpassed.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi tāta sukhād eva sukham eṣyasi śobhanam sukhāt sukhataraprāptim āpnute matimān naraḥ
english: For you, dear one, will pass from happiness to lovely happiness; from happiness to the gaining of a greater happiness does the wise man attain.

sanskrit: tan naḥ pratyakṣam evedam upalabdham asaṃśayam śrīmantam āpnuvanty arthā dānaṃ yajñas tathā sukham
english: This is plain to our very sight, grasped beyond doubt: riches attain the man of fortune, and so do giving, and sacrifice, and ease.

sanskrit: sukhād eva paraṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhād anyat paraṃ sukham dṛśyate hi mahāprājña niyataṃ vai svabhāvataḥ
english: From happiness comes a further sorrow, and from sorrow another, higher happiness; for so it is seen, O greatly wise one, fixed by its very nature.

sanskrit: trividhānīha vṛttāni narasyāhur manīṣiṇaḥ puṇyam anyat pāpam anyan na puṇyaṃ na ca pāpakam
english: Threefold, the wise declare, are the courses of a man's conduct here: one is meritorious, another sinful, and one neither meritorious nor sinful.

sanskrit: na vṛttaṃ manyate 'nyasya manyate 'nyasya pāpakam tathā svakarmanirvṛttaṃ na puṇyaṃ na ca pāpakam
english: He approves not the conduct of one man, and deems another's sinful; so too, that which arises from one's own appointed work is neither meritorious nor sinful.

sanskrit: ramasvaidhasva modasva dehi caiva yajasva ca na tvām abhibhaviṣyanti vaidyā na ca tapasvinaḥ
english: Delight, prosper, rejoice, and give, and sacrifice too: neither the learned in lore nor the practisers of austerity shall overmaster you.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca maitreyaḥ karmapūjakaḥ atyantaṃ śrīmati kule jātaḥ prājño bahuśrutaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, Maitreya, who honored action—born in a most illustrious family, wise and deeply learned—made reply.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ mahāprājña yathaivāttha tathaiva tat anujñātas tu bhavatā kiṃ cid brūyām ahaṃ vibho
english: Beyond doubt, O greatly wise one, it is just as you have said; yet with your leave, mighty one, I would say a word.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yad yad icchasi maitreya yāvad yāvad yathā tathā brūhi tāvan mahāprājña śuśrūṣe vacanaṃ tava
english: Vyāsa said: Whatever you wish, Maitreya, however much and in whatever way—speak it, O greatly wise one; I would gladly hear your words.

sanskrit: maitreya uvāca nirdoṣaṃ nirmalaṃ caiva vacanaṃ dānasaṃhitam vidyātapobhyāṃ hi bhavān bhāvitātmā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Maitreya said: Faultless and unblemished is your speech, charged with the praise of giving; for by learning and austerity your self is purified—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bhavato bhāvitātmatvād dāyo 'yaṃ sumahān mama bhūyo buddhyānupaśyāmi susamṛddhatapā iva
english: Because your self is so purified, this gift of mine becomes very great; the more I consider it with my mind, the more it seems like the fruit of richly accomplished austerity.

sanskrit: api me darśanād eva bhavato 'bhyudayo mahān manye bhavatprasādo 'yaṃ tad dhi karma svabhāvataḥ
english: From the mere sight of you, indeed, great prosperity comes to me; I deem this your grace—for such is action by its very nature.

sanskrit: tapaḥ śrutaṃ ca yoniś cāpy etad brāhmaṇyakāraṇam tribhir guṇaiḥ samuditas tato bhavati vai dvijaḥ
english: Austerity, sacred learning, and high birth—these are the grounds of brahmanhood; endowed with these three qualities, a man then becomes a twice-born indeed.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tṛpte ca tṛpyante pitaro daivatāni ca na hi śrutavatāṃ kiṃ cid adhikaṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte
english: When such a one is satisfied, the ancestors and the gods are satisfied too; for among those rich in learning there is nothing higher than a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: yathā hi sukṛte kṣetre phalaṃ vindati mānavaḥ evaṃ dattvā śrutavati phalaṃ dātā samaśnute
english: For just as a man reaps fruit from a well-tilled field, so the giver, having given to one rich in learning, enjoys his fruit.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaś cen na vidyeta śrutavṛttopasaṃhitaḥ pratigrahītā dānasya moghaṃ syād dhanināṃ dhanam
english: Were there no brāhmaṇa endowed with learning and good conduct to be the receiver of a gift, the wealth of the wealthy would be in vain.

sanskrit: adan hy avidvān hanty annam adyamānaṃ ca hanti tam taṃ ca hanyati yasyānnaṃ sa hatvā hanyate 'budhaḥ
english: For an ignorant man, eating, destroys the food, and the food being eaten destroys him; and he destroys the one whose food it was—thus destroying, the fool is himself destroyed.

sanskrit: prabhur hy annam adan vidvān punar janayatīśvaraḥ sa cānnāj jāyate tasmāt sūkṣma eva vyatikramaḥ
english: But the learned man, the master, eating food, the capable one, brings it forth again; and he himself is born of food—hence the transition between them is a subtle one.

sanskrit: yad eva dadataḥ puṇyaṃ tad eva pratigṛhṇataḥ na hy ekacakraṃ varteta ity evam ṛṣayo viduḥ
english: The very merit of the giver is the merit of the receiver; for a single wheel cannot roll—thus the seers have understood.

sanskrit: yatra vai brāhmaṇāḥ santi śrutavṛttopasaṃhitāḥ tatra dānaphalaṃ puṇyam iha cāmutra cāśnute
english: Where there are brāhmaṇas endowed with learning and good conduct, there the giver enjoys the meritorious fruit of his gift, both here and in the world beyond.

sanskrit: ye yoniśuddhāḥ satataṃ tapasy abhiratā bhṛśam dānādhyayanasaṃpannās te vai pūjyatamāḥ sadā
english: Those who are pure in birth, ever ardently devoted to austerity, accomplished in giving and in study—they indeed are most worthy of worship always.

sanskrit: tair hi sadbhiḥ kṛtaḥ panthāś cetayāno na muhyate te hi svargasya netāro yajñavāhāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: For the path made by those good men—he who is mindful of it does not go astray; for they are the guides to heaven, the eternal bearers of sacrifice.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktaḥ sa bhagavān maitreyaṃ pratyabhāṣata diṣṭyaivaṃ tvaṃ vijānāsi diṣṭyā te buddhir īdṛśī loko hy ayaṃ guṇān eva bhūyiṣṭhaṃ sma praśaṃsati
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the venerable one answered Maitreya in turn: Happily do you understand things thus; happily is your understanding such! For this world, for the most part, praises only the virtues.

sanskrit: rūpamānavayomānaśrīmānāś cāpy asaṃśayam diṣṭyā nābhibhavanti tvāṃ daivas te 'yam anugrahaḥ yat te bhṛśataraṃ dānād vartayiṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: Pride of beauty, pride of age, and pride of fortune—undoubtedly, happily, these do not overmaster you; this is heaven's grace upon you. Now hear what I shall set forth as even higher than giving.

sanskrit: yānīhāgamaśāstrāṇi yāś ca kāś cit pravṛttayaḥ tāni vedaṃ puraskṛtya pravṛttāni yathākramam
english: Whatever scriptures of tradition there are here, and whatever undertakings of any kind, these have all proceeded, each in its order, with the Veda set before them.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dānaṃ praśaṃsāmi bhavān api tapaḥśrute tapaḥ pavitraṃ vedasya tapaḥ svargasya sādhanam
english: I extol giving, and you extol austerity and sacred learning; austerity is the sanctifier of the Veda, austerity is the means to heaven.

sanskrit: tapasā mahad āpnoti vidyayā ceti naḥ śrutam tapasaiva cāpanuded yac cānyad api duṣkṛtam
english: By austerity one attains greatness, and by knowledge—so we have heard; and by austerity alone one may wipe away whatever other evil has been done.

sanskrit: yad yad dhi kiṃ cit saṃdhāya puruṣas tapyate tapaḥ sarvam etad avāpnoti brāhmaṇo vedapāragaḥ
english: For whatever a man, fixing his aim, performs austerity for, all this the brāhmaṇa who has crossed to the far shore of the Veda attains.

sanskrit: duranvayaṃ duṣpradhṛṣyaṃ durāpaṃ duratikramam sarvaṃ vai tapasābhyeti tapo hi balavattaram
english: What is hard to follow, hard to assail, hard to win, hard to overcome—all of it one reaches through austerity; for austerity is the mightier power.

sanskrit: surāpo 'saṃmatādāyī bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ tapasā tarate sarvam enasaś ca pramucyate
english: The drinker of liquor, the taker of what was not granted, the slayer of an embryo, the defiler of his teacher's bed—through austerity he crosses over all, and is released from his sin.

sanskrit: sarvavidyas tu cakṣuṣmān api yādṛśatādṛśaḥ tapasvinau ca tāv āhus tābhyāṃ kāryaṃ sadā namaḥ
english: The man of all knowledge, the man of clear sight, of whatever rank he be—both these they call ascetics, and to both reverence should ever be made.

sanskrit: sarve pūjyāḥ śrutadhanās tathaiva ca tapasvinaḥ dānapradāḥ sukhaṃ pretya prāpnuvantīha ca śriyam
english: All who are rich in sacred learning are worthy of worship, and so too the ascetics; the givers of gifts attain happiness after death, and fortune here below.

sanskrit: imaṃ ca brahmalokaṃ ca lokaṃ ca balavattaram annadānaiḥ sukṛtinaḥ pratipadyanti laukikāḥ
english: This world, and the world of Brahmā, and the mightier world beyond—by gifts of food the well-doing folk of this world attain them all.

sanskrit: pūjitāḥ pūjayanty etān mānitā mānayanti ca adātā yatra yatraiti sarvataḥ saṃpraṇudyate
english: Being honored, men honor these in return; being esteemed, they give esteem; but the non-giver, wherever he goes, is on every side thrust away.

sanskrit: akartā caiva kartā ca labhate yasya yādṛśam yady evordhvaṃ yady avāk ca tvaṃ lokam abhiyāsyasi
english: The doer and the non-doer alike obtain each what his deeds deserve; whether you go upward or downward to your world hereafter—

sanskrit: prāpsyase tv annapānāni yāni dāsyasi kāni cit medhāvy asi kule jātaḥ śrutavān anṛśaṃsavān
english: —you will obtain such food and drink as you may give. You are wise, nobly born, learned, and free from cruelty.

sanskrit: kaumāradāravratavān maitreya nirato bhava etad gṛhāṇa prathamaṃ praśastaṃ gṛhamedhinām
english: Holding the vow of taking a wife in your youth, O Maitreya, be devoted to it; embrace this first, the course commended for householders.

sanskrit: yo bhartā vāsitātuṣṭo bhartus tuṣṭā ca vāsitā yasminn evaṃ kule sarvaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tatra vartate
english: Where the husband is content with his wife and the wife content with her husband—in that household where it is so, all that is good prevails.

sanskrit: adbhir gātrān malam iva tamo 'gniprabhayā yathā dānena tapasā caiva sarvapāpam apohyate
english: As dirt is washed from the limbs by water, as darkness is dispelled by the light of fire, so by giving and by austerity all sin is driven away.

sanskrit: svasti prāpnuhi maitreya gṛhān sādhu vrajāmy aham etan manasi kartavyaṃ śreya evaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Fare you well, Maitreya; I now take my leave and go to my dwelling. Keep this in mind, and so your welfare shall come to be.

sanskrit: taṃ praṇamyātha maitreyaḥ kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam svasti prāpnotu bhagavān ity uvāca kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Then Maitreya bowed to him and walked round him keeping him to the right, and with hands joined in reverence said, "May the venerable one fare well."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca satstrīṇāṃ samudācāraṃ sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ tvattas taṃ me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The course of conduct of virtuous women, O best of all upholders of dharma, I wish to hear from you; tell it to me, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvajñāṃ sarvadharmajñāṃ devaloke manasvinīm kaikeyī sumanā nāma śāṇḍilīṃ paryapṛcchata
english: Bhīṣma said: In the world of the gods, a Kaikeyī princess named Sumanā questioned Śāṇḍilī—the all-knowing, the knower of every dharma, the high-minded woman.

sanskrit: kena vṛttena kalyāṇi samācāreṇa kena vā vidhūya sarvapāpāni devalokaṃ tvam āgatā
english: By what conduct, O fair one, or by what course of life, having shaken off all sins, have you come to the world of the gods?

sanskrit: hutāśanaśikheva tvaṃ jvalamānā svatejasā sutā tārādhipasyeva prabhayā divam āgatā
english: Blazing with your own splendor like the tongue of the fire-god, you have come to heaven by your radiance, as though you were the daughter of the moon, the lord of stars.

sanskrit: arajāṃsi ca vastrāṇi dhārayantī gataklamā vimānasthā śubhe bhāsi sahasraguṇam ojasā
english: Wearing spotless garments, free of all weariness, seated in your celestial car, you shine, O lovely one, with a thousandfold strength of light.

sanskrit: na tvam alpena tapasā dānena niyamena vā imaṃ lokam anuprāptā tasmāt tattvaṃ vadasva me
english: Not by any small austerity, nor giving, nor self-restraint have you attained this world; therefore tell me the truth of it.

sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭā sumanayā madhuraṃ cāruhāsinī śāṇḍilī nibhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ sumanām idam abravīt
english: Thus questioned by Sumanā, Śāṇḍilī of the sweet and lovely smile spoke this measured word to Sumanā:

sanskrit: nāhaṃ kāṣāyavasanā nāpi valkaladhāriṇī na ca muṇḍā na jaṭilā bhūtvā devatvam āgatā
english: Not by becoming a wearer of ochre robes, nor of bark garments, nor shaven-headed, nor matted-haired did I attain to godhood.

sanskrit: ahitāni ca vākyāni sarvāṇi paruṣāṇi ca apramattā ca bhartāraṃ kadā cin nāham abruvam
english: Words unkind, and all words that were harsh—heedful, I never at any time spoke them to my husband.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca pūjane apramattā sadāyuktā śvaśrūśvaśuravartinī
english: In the worship of the gods, the ancestors, and the brāhmaṇas I was ever heedful and intent, devoted to my mother-in-law and father-in-law.

sanskrit: paiśunye na pravartāmi na mamaitan manogatam advāre na ca tiṣṭhāmi ciraṃ na kathayāmi ca
english: I never engaged in slander, nor did such a thing enter my mind; I did not loiter where there was no doorway, nor talk for long.

sanskrit: asad vā hasitaṃ kiṃ cid ahitaṃ vāpi karmaṇā rahasyam arahasyaṃ vā na pravartāmi sarvathā
english: Any unseemly laughter, or anything hurtful in deed, secret or open—in this I never engaged at all.

sanskrit: kāryārthe nirgataṃ cāpi bhartāraṃ gṛham āgatam āsanenopasaṃyojya pūjayāmi samāhitā
english: And my husband, gone out on some errand and returned home, I would settle on a seat and honor with collected mind.

sanskrit: yad yac ca nābhijānāti yad bhojyaṃ nābhinandati bhakṣyaṃ vāpy atha vā lehyaṃ tat sarvaṃ varjayāmy aham
english: And whatever he did not recognize, whatever food he did not relish, whether to be chewed or to be licked—all that I would set aside.

sanskrit: kuṭumbārthe samānītaṃ yat kiṃ cit kāryam eva tu prātar utthāya tat sarvaṃ kārayāmi karomi ca
english: Whatever task there was, brought together for the household's sake, rising at dawn I would have all of it done, and did it myself.

sanskrit: pravāsaṃ yadi me bhartā yāti kāryeṇa kena cit maṅgalair bahubhir yuktā bhavāmi niyatā sadā
english: If my husband went abroad on some business, I would devote myself, ever restrained, to many auspicious observances.

sanskrit: añjanaṃ rocanāṃ caiva snānaṃ mālyānulepanam prasādhanaṃ ca niṣkrānte nābhinandāmi bhartari
english: Eye-salve and yellow pigment, bathing, garlands and unguents, and adornment—when my husband had gone out, in none of these did I take delight.

sanskrit: notthāpayāmi bhartāraṃ sukhasuptam ahaṃ sadā ātureṣv api kāryeṣu tena tuṣyati me manaḥ
english: I never roused my husband when he was sleeping at ease, even in pressing tasks; and by that my mind found contentment.

sanskrit: nāyāsayāmi bhartāraṃ kuṭumbārthe ca sarvadā guptaguhyā sadā cāsmi susaṃmṛṣṭaniveśanā
english: I never wearied my husband over household matters at any time; ever I kept secrets well-guarded, and my dwelling well-swept and clean.

sanskrit: imaṃ dharmapathaṃ nārī pālayantī samāhitā arundhatīva nārīṇāṃ svargaloke mahīyate
english: A woman who guards this path of dharma with a collected mind is exalted in heaven among women, like Arundhatī.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etad ākhyāya sā devī sumanāyai tapasvinī patidharmaṃ mahābhāgā jagāmādarśanaṃ tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Having declared to Sumanā this dharma of devotion to one's husband, that goddess, the ascetic and greatly blessed lady, then passed from sight.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ pāṇḍavākhyānaṃ paṭhet parvaṇi parvaṇi sa devalokaṃ saṃprāpya nandane susukhaṃ vaset
english: And whoever reads this tale told to the Pāṇḍava, at each parva-juncture, will reach the world of the gods and dwell in supreme bliss in the Nandana grove.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sāmnā vāpi pradāne vā jyāyaḥ kiṃ bhavato matam prabrūhi bharataśreṣṭha yad atra vyatiricyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By conciliation or by giving—which do you hold the better? Declare to me, O best of the Bharatas, which of the two prevails here.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sāmnā prasādyate kaś cid dānena ca tathāparaḥ puruṣaḥ prakṛtiṃ jñātvā tayor ekataraṃ bhajet
english: Bhīṣma said: One man is won over by conciliation, and another by a gift; having understood a man's nature, one should resort to one of these two.

sanskrit: guṇāṃs tu śṛṇu me rājan sāntvasya bharatarṣabha dāruṇāny api bhūtāni sāntvenārādhayed yathā
english: But hear from me, O king, the virtues of gentle speech, O bull of the Bharatas—how even fierce creatures may be propitiated by gentleness.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gṛhītvā rakṣasā mukto dvijātiḥ kānane yathā
english: On this they cite an ancient tale: how a twice-born man, seized by a rākṣasa in the forest, was set free.

sanskrit: kaś cit tu buddhisaṃpanno brāhmaṇo vijane vane gṛhītaḥ kṛcchram āpanno rakṣasā bhakṣayiṣyatā
english: A certain brāhmaṇa, endowed with intelligence, in a lonely wood was seized and brought to a sore strait by a rākṣasa about to devour him.

sanskrit: sa buddhiśrutasaṃpannas taṃ dṛṣṭvātīva bhīṣaṇam sāmaivāsmin prayuyuje na mumoha na vivyathe
english: He, endowed with intelligence and learning, beholding that exceedingly terrible being, employed gentle speech upon him; he neither lost his wits nor trembled.
